 Shivam Yadav

 Appearance:
Shri S.K.Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Harish Sharma, learned Government Advocate for respon  Shri Jitendra Tyagi, learned counsel for complainant.
ORDER 1.

The present petition has been preferred by petitioners under Section 528 of the BNSS for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.92/2022 registered at Police Station Badoni, District Datia for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and Section 7/8 of POCSO Act whereby case vide ST.No.41/2024 pending before Second Addtional Sessions Judge, Datia as well as entire consequential proceedings arising out of the same.
2. Petitioner and complainant along with respondent No.3 have already appeared on 25.02.2025 before Principal Registrar to ink down their identity.

Petitioner and respondent No.3 entered into wedlock and this fact has been verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court also therefore, it is clear that petitioner No.1 and respondent No.3 are married couple and blessed with one child.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5668 2 MCRC-2822-2025 3.
Posecutrix/respondent No.3 stated that they got married on their own volition and are blessed with one child.

sentences.text:
Therefore, they filed applications vide I.A. No.1198/2025 and I.A.
No.1199/2024 for compounding the offence on the basis of compromise.
The report of Principal Registrar of this Court is on record.
4. Counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer.
However, could not dispute the factum regarding compromise.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
6.
This is a case where petitioner and respondent No.3/prosecutrix shared emotional and physical proximity.
At the instance of father of prosecutrix, case was registered against petitioner.
Petitioner and respondent No.3 entered into wedlock.
They earlier appeared before Principal Registrar of this Court and expressed their desire for settlement.

7. Be that as it may.
8.
Fact remains that petitioner and respondent No.3 are married couple and both are living in same household and they are blessed with one child.
It is regular and easy to be retributive but at the same time a Judge has to sublimely feel the pulse of the case.

One cannot forget that "Every "F I L E"
with same alphabets, contains a "L I F E".

(See : In Re State of Madhya Pradesh Vs.
Pankaj Mishra, 2021 SCC OnLine MP 5480 and Geeta Paliwal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5668 3 MCRC-2822-2025 and others Vs. Sitaram and others reported as 2023 SCC Online MP 811.).
9.

sentences.text: Here "FILE" before this Court carries not only a "LIFE" but many LIVES.

10. Therefore, applications vide I.A. No.1198/2025 and I.A. No.1199/2025 are hereby allowed and this Court under the obtaining facts and circumstances of the case intends to tread on the path of reformative or atleast other than retributive one because:-
(i) A girl of tender age around (16-17 years) has fallen in love with a boy of (20-21)
years and driven by hormones they shared emotional and physical proximity and moved out of social/legal limits.
(ii) Girl was of consistent view that she shared emotional/physical proximity on her own volition and she left her maternal home voluntarily.
Her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. indicate so.
(iii) Petitioner and prosecutrix entered into wedlock and girl/prosecutrix is living peacefully with her husband.
They are blessed with one child.
In case of any punishment, petitioner may have to go to jail and that would disrupt the family forever.

2 (iv)

sentences.text: Both the parties appeared before the Principal Registrar of this Court and inked down their intent and identity repeatedly.
Therefore, in the cumulative facts and circumstances of the case, matter deserves consideration.
(v) Petitioner does not have any previous criminal background so as to infer any mischief at this juncture.

Therefore, keeping this spirit, this Court intends to inject "
L I F E" into this "F I L E" in the interest of justice.

11. Resultantly, the petition stands allowed on the basis of compromise and FIR bearing Crime No.92/2022 registered at Police Station Badoni, District Datia for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and Section 7/8 of POCSO Act whereby case vide ST.No.41/2024 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5668 4 MCRC-2822-2025 pending before Second Addtional Sessions Judge, Datia, as well as entire consequential proceedings arising therefrom,
stand quashed.
Petitioner is set free.

But an expectation can certainly be raised by this Court that petitioner and prosecutrix shall live peacefully and would try to attain nuptial bliss so that family and social harmony can be maintained.
12. Petition stands disposed of.

(ANAND PATHAK) (HARISH  MEMBER MEMB  Ashish*
